implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a function that can suspend, saving its state, and resume later from wherever the scheduler decides - possibly on a different thread. Two flavours: STACKFUL, which keeps an independent call stack so any function can suspend at any depth (Go goroutines, Java virtual threads, Lua coroutines) and avoids the 'function colouring' problem; and STACKLESS, which stores the locals and resume point in a heap state object so a suspension can only happen in a function declared suspend, and the colour propagates up the call chain. Both compose the same way: give every coroutine a scope, suspend only at points that can wait, never block the carrier thread, and make cancellation cooperative and observable.
idiom_name: suspend/resume with a saved state - stackful (independent stack) or stackless (heap state object + state machine)
code_sketch:
# The discipline, language-neutral:
#
#   coroutine(scope):                  # the scope bounds its lifetime
#       try:
#           user   = await get(id)     # suspension point: state saved, thread freed
#           orders = await fetch(user)  # straight-line code, not nested callbacks
#           return [o for o in orders if o.ready]
#       except Cancelled:
#           cleanup(); raise             # cancellation is a control signal, not an error
#
# Stackful:   any function may suspend at any call depth (Go, virtual threads, Lua)
# Stackless:  only a `suspend` function may suspend, and every caller must be
#             `suspend` too - the 'function colouring' the compiler enforces.
#
# Never block the carrier: a synchronous read inside the body occupies the
# thread and can deadlock a bounded pool.
pitfalls: Blocking the carrier thread (a sync read or a CPU loop) deadlocks a bounded pool - this is the characteristic failure.
Launching with no scope makes the work outlive its request and invisible to cancellation.
Swallowing cancellation as an ordinary error leaves the coroutine running and its resources un-released.
A coroutine resumes on a different thread, so thread-local state does not travel across a suspension unless context is propagated explicitly.
